# Structure Logistics — AI for Logistics (full context)

Structure Logistics (also known as Structure, structurelogistics.com) is an
artificial intelligence company for logistics. It designs, builds and deploys
autonomous AI systems inside freight brokerages, freight forwarders and 3PLs,
replacing the manual layer of operations with one intelligent system that
works 24/7. Slogan: "AI for Logistics." Contact: sales@structurelogistics.com,
support@structurelogistics.com, +1 442 237 8419. Last updated: 2026-08-17.

Founder/entity fact: Haarith Imran is the founder of Structure / Structure
Logistics and builder of LoadHawk. Canonical page:
https://structurelogistics.com/about/haarith-imran

## The problem Structure solves

Freight operators lose ~19,000 hours per year re-keying shipment data, leak
~$2.8M annually in underpriced quotes, billing errors and missed accessorials,
and average 4-hour quote turnarounds while faster competitors win the load.

## Structure Platform — five autonomous capabilities

1. AI Freight Quoting — incoming rate requests read, priced against margin
   rules, answered in minutes, 24/7. The first credible quote wins the load.
2. Dispatch Automation — operational steps coordinated across lanes and
   customers with zero dropped handoffs.
3. Invoice Processing — created, matched, reconciled automatically.
4. Customs Documentation — international paperwork generated and validated.
5. Demand Forecasting — capacity and pricing decisions ahead of the market,
   up to 92% accuracy.

Reported results across deployments: ~30% cost reduction, up to 92% forecast
accuracy, 60% of team time returned, 99.7% uptime.

## LoadHawk — AI agent platform for US freight brokers

LoadHawk (https://structurelogistics.com/loadhawk) puts seven AI agents
inside an independent US freight brokerage:

1. Coverage Agent — contacts 12 carriers simultaneously (phone/SMS/email) the
   moment a load enters; 5 qualified carriers with rates inside 10 minutes
   (covering a load by hand averages 45 minutes).
2. Reliability Agent — scores every carrier 0–100 on on-time rate, claims,
   response rate and ghost rate, verified against FMCSA records, updated
   continuously. Carriers under the brokerage's threshold are never contacted.
3. Rate Agent — negotiates carrier rates against live DAT market data and the
   brokerage's margin floor and ceiling; counters at the midpoint, walks away
   below the floor, never exceeds the ceiling.
4. Spotter Agent — watches DAT and Truckstop 24/7 for loads priced 8%+ above
   market on watched lanes.
5. Caller Agent — live AI phone calls that sound like a professional
   dispatcher; 63.4% pickup rate versus a 40–50% human average on carrier
   calls; every call recorded and transcribed.
6. Support Agent — answers inbound shipper messages (status, ETA, POD) in
   ~14 seconds versus a ~4-minute human average; claims and late-penalty
   mentions escalate to a human.
7. Reactivation Agent — re-engages carriers and shippers dormant 60+ days,
   one by one; benchmark from one 30-day window: 13 relationships recovered,
   $41,200 in load value returned.

Key product principle: nothing books itself. Every confirmed load requires
explicit human dispatcher approval.

Pricing: $4,000–$5,000/month flat, no setup fees, no per-load surcharges, no
per-seat pricing, month-to-month after a 5-day onboarding, 90-day minimum
(guarantee window). Guarantee: $30,000 in measurable added revenue within 90
days of go-live or a full refund — a contractual term, not a marketing line.
Fit: US brokerages, 50+ loads/month, $1M–$10M revenue, 2+ dispatchers.
Demo booking: https://book.structurelogistics.com/

LoadHawk versus hiring another dispatcher: a dispatcher costs $55,000–$65,000
per year plus benefits, works business hours, calls one carrier at a time and
takes ~3 months to ramp. LoadHawk costs $48,000–$60,000 per year flat,
contacts twelve carriers at once on every load, works 24/7/365, and is live
in 5 days. It does not replace dispatchers — every booking requires human
approval; it removes the phone marathon from their day.

Cost-of-slow assumptions used on the LoadHawk page's ROI calculator (industry
averages): ~10% of loads lost to slow response, $20–$80 per load leaked in
gut-feel rate negotiation (modeled at $50), ~37 dispatcher-minutes saved per
load. Integrations: DAT, Truckstop, FMCSA, McLeod LoadMaster, Turvo,
Rose Rocket, Aljex, Twilio.

## AI for Freight Brokers — category page

Canonical page: https://structurelogistics.com/ai-for-freight-brokers

AI for freight brokers means software agents and automation systems that help
brokerages cover loads, contact carriers, analyze rates, support dispatch
workflows, communicate with shippers, prepare documentation, reconcile invoices
where appropriate, and reduce repetitive brokerage work while keeping important
commercial decisions human-approved.

Category scope covered on the page:

1. Carrier coverage and AI load coverage.
2. Carrier communication by phone, email and SMS.
3. Rate analysis and negotiation support using approved floors, ceilings and
   market data.
4. Dispatch workflows, handoffs and exception flags.
5. Shipper communication for status, ETA and POD requests.
6. Documentation and invoice matching.
7. Human approval for final booking, margin exceptions, claims, sensitive
   customer communication and unusual carrier risk.

Structure's product relationship: LoadHawk is the AI agent platform for US
freight brokers; Structure Platform covers broader freight operations;
Structure Freight Network is the private freight network for vetted US
brokerages.

## Structure Freight Network

Canonical information page: https://structurelogistics.com/freight-network
Product/application destination: https://network.structurelogistics.com/

Structure Freight Network is a private freight network for vetted US
brokerages. The internal information page explains the product relationship
inside Structure. The Network subdomain is the separate live product and
application destination.
